sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A briefing for the WestCap CISO Summit, and a page for the people met there.
sections.para: The summit, 20 to 22 October in New York, has panels on AI governance, AI attacks and AI for defence. An Agent Behaviour Policy writes down what an agent can do, may do, and what stands in the way; only a rule out of its reach is a control. Here it is said for six kinds of person, with what to read.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Seven points: the summit, the policy, the test, the offer, early access, six rooms, open.
sections.para: The summit is about modern defence, with AI running through it. A policy writes down what an agent can and may do, and what stands in the way. Only a rule kept out of reach is a control. RiskMandate sells the policy, £10 to £1,500, paid once; early users get help at no cost. All of it is open.

sections.label: The summit
sections.line: The summit: three days, five panels, a Shark Tank.
sections.para: Tuesday is for WestCap's portfolio, on business-risk alignment and operational security. Wednesday has five panels, three about AI: governance, preparing for an AI attack, and AI for defence. Thursday, six startups pitch. The companies on the panels map the room: compliance, data security, supply chain, incident response, offensive security, AI defence.

sections.label: What we do, in three sentences
sections.line: What we do, in three sentences, and the four words.
sections.para: An Agent Behaviour Policy describes, for one agent in one deployment, everything it can do, what it was authorised to do, the difference, and what stands in the way. RiskMandate writes it for the agent you run. The grant, mandate, delta and barrier; only a boundary kept out of the agent's reach is a control.

sections.label: Said for each kind of person
sections.line: The same idea, said for six kinds of person.
sections.para: For CISOs: what each agent can reach and what stops it. For governance and audit: logs are a self-report. For incident response: incidents are reach beyond mandate. For AI-for-defence vendors: their agents need a policy too. For investors: liability needs a written line. For founders: start selling what you have. Each with articles and vaults.

sections.label: Where we add value
sections.line: Where we add value: what guardrails are compiled from.
sections.para: Most of the room sells something that acts at runtime. A policy is what those are configured from: it tells a gateway which rules to keep, an auditor what to test, a responder where to look and an insurer what contains the agent. It sits alongside them. It is open: CC BY 4.0 for policies, Apache 2.0 for code.

sections.label: Next steps
sections.line: Next steps: read, pick one agent, join early access.
sections.para: Read the explainer and one article from your section. Pick one agent; the policy is per agent, per deployment. Join early access, where we build and correct the policy with you at no cost, in exchange for telling us where it is wrong. Or buy a level, £10 to £1,500, paid once. Or talk to us.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: What this briefing does not claim.
sections.para: We are not part of the summit's programme. No speaker is quoted; panels and companies are from the public agenda. How each company fits is our reading. Two of the four levels had not been sold by mid-September. The vaults are illustrative, with invented organisations and numbers.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.para: The summit's public page, riskmandate.ai with its pricing and early access pages, and abp.sgit.ai, all read on 20 October 2026, and the articles and vaults linked in each section.
